tagline: Biggs to Baker City by way of the John Day country.
intro: The byway leaves Biggs, where Oregon Trail travelers first saw the Columbia, and climbs south through farm country to Moro and Shaniko, then over to Antelope and Fossil. At Service Creek it meets the John Day River, which keeps it company for about 100 miles through Spray and the John Day Canyon to Dayville and the town of John Day.

Past Prairie City, OR 7 climbs northeast into the foothills of the Blue Mountains, past the old railroad logging town of Austin, and comes down at last to Baker City, the end of the byway's 286 miles from the Columbia.
season: TripCheck lists it as a year-round drive.

moments.title: Shaniko
moments.text: The railroad from Biggs made Shaniko the Wool Capital of the World in the early 1900s, and a quicker line up the Deschutes canyon in 1911 started it toward ghost town.

moments.title: Fossil
moments.text: Named by its first postmaster for the fossils he found on his ranch, the town keeps a public collecting site where anyone may dig for leaf imprints.

moments.title: Kam Wah Chung & Co. Museum
moments.text: Doc Hay asked that his Chinese herbal apothecary go to the city as a museum, and after he died in 1952 the wish and the city's ownership were both forgotten until 1967.
